title: Optimization Landscape Geometry in VQE for Frustrated Quantum Spin Models
authors: Vojtěch Novák, Ivan Zelinka, Swagatam Das, Martin Beseda
abstract: We benchmark eight classical optimizers for exact-statevector VQE calculations on a controlled hierarchy of frustrated spin models, ranging from a diagonal Ising glass to transverse-field Ising and anisotropic Heisenberg models. The benchmark includes local, stochastic-gradient, evolutionary, covariance-adaptation, and swarm-based optimization methods under matched function-evaluation budgets. To understand their performance beyond final energies, we characterize the underlying Hamiltonian--ansatz landscapes in terms of local minima, gradients, curvature, and ground-state reachability. We use simple variational circuits, from an $R_y$ product-state ansatz for the diagonal model to shallow $R_y$--CNOT hardware-efficient circuits for the noncommuting models, and study how increasing circuit depth changes their expressivity, reachability, and optimization geometry. We find that optimizer performance changes substantially across the model hierarchy and is closely connected to landscape structure, while the variational gap represents a separate source of error. These results show how classical optimization, variational expressivity, and landscape geometry jointly determine VQE performance for frustrated spin models.
summary: This work rigorously benchmarks various classical optimization algorithms for VQE applied to frustrated quantum spin models. By characterizing the geometry of the energy landscape, the authors demonstrate that optimization performance is highly dependent on the model structure and that the total error budget must account separately for optimization failure and the inherent variational gap. This guides the development of more robust quantum simulation protocols.
main_problem: The paper benchmarks classical optimization algorithms for Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) calculations to understand how the underlying Hamiltonian-ansatz landscape geometry dictates performance.
main_result: Optimizer performance varies significantly across different frustrated spin model hierarchies, and the study successfully separates optimization error from the inherent variational gap error.
method: The authors benchmark eight classical optimizers (local, stochastic, evolutionary, etc.) using exact statevector simulation on controlled spin models, characterizing the energy landscape geometry.
model_or_system: The study uses frustrated quantum spin models, including diagonal Ising glasses, transverse-field Ising, and anisotropic Heisenberg models. The Hamiltonian is parameterized to cover these different physical regimes.
key_observables: Optimization error ($\Delta E_{	ext{opt}}$), ground-state energy error ($\Delta E$), and the variational gap ($E_{	ext{ref}} - E_0$). Fidelity is also used as a diagnostic.
important_parameters: The comparison involves varying circuit depth (from product-state to hardware-efficient ansatz) and the model parameters ($\Gamma, \lambda$) defining the Hamiltonian.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on exact statevector simulation to isolate the intrinsic landscape from finite-shot noise, and it distinguishes between optimization difficulty and variational expressivity limits.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the two ansatz architectures (product-state vs. hardware-efficient) used for the different models.
paper_structure: The paper systematically benchmarks optimizers across a hierarchy of frustrated spin models (Q1, Q2, Q3), characterizing the landscape geometry and quantifying the sources of error in VQE performance.
why_interesting: It provides a deep, quantitative analysis of the limitations of classical optimization techniques when applied to complex, frustrated quantum many-body systems, which is crucial for designing practical quantum algorithms.

Depth improves physical reachability, while the deeper landscapes remain strongly anisotropic. The random-gradient scale decreases with depth but remains finite over the studied range.
